units.title: Single-block precision: the literal formula (4)
units.statement: For every natural dimension n, real parameter kappa and real orthogonal matrix O, define A_O by the displayed expression. The definition is algebraic on the whole carrier; the regularity theorem retains the source standing range n>=3 and kappa>=4.
assumptions: n is a natural number; κ is real.
O is an n by n real orthogonal matrix; both determinant signs are allowed.

steps.title: Retain the coefficients and transpose
steps.text: The identity coefficient is (kappa+1)/2, while the coefficient of O+O^T is -(kappa-1)/4. The definition contains no precomputed spectral estimate.
steps.lean: The body is exactly the scalar multiples, matrix addition, transpose and subtraction shown in the formula.

units.lean_statement: A literal matrix-valued definition on every n, κ and O.
units.lean_proof: No existence or fallback branch: this is the displayed algebraic expression.
units.boundary: Only the single-block equation (26). Full block diagonal assembly, Gaussian normalization, unique minimizer and both query-complexity lower bounds remain open.

units.title: Orthogonality and Cauchy–Schwarz give the single-block spectral bounds
units.statement: Let n>=3, kappa>=4 and O belong to the real orthogonal group O(n). The matrix A_O in equation (4) is real symmetric, and every real vector v satisfies v^T v <= v^T A_O v <= kappa v^T v. This is the quadratic-form formulation of source equation (26).
assumptions: n≥3 and κ≥4 are the standing range in Section 3.1.
O belongs to the full real orthogonal group O(n).
The bounds hold for every real coordinate vector, including zero.

steps.title: Orthogonality preserves the Euclidean squared norm
steps.text: Use O^T O=I to reduce (Ov)^T(Ov) to v^T v. Squared Euclidean norms are represented by sums of squared coordinates.
steps.lean: horth uses Matrix.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff'; hiso uses the transpose dot-product identity and matrix multiplication.

steps.title: Control the cross term
steps.text: Finite-sum Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the square of the cross term. Together with v^T v>=0 this gives both signed inequalities. These estimates are derived inside the proof.
steps.lean: hcs applies Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq; hcross derives the two real bounds.

steps.title: Expand the quadratic form
steps.text: Over the reals, v^T O^T v equals v^T O v, so the two transpose cross terms combine.
steps.lean: htranspose is Matrix.dotProduct_transpose_mulVec; hexpand distributes mulVec and dotProduct and checks the coefficient algebra.

steps.title: Scale with the correct sign and prove symmetry
steps.text: The standing kappa>=4 implies (kappa-1)/2>=0. Substituting the upper and lower cross-term bounds gives the lower and upper quadratic bounds respectively. Transpose fixes both I and O+O^T, hence A_O is symmetric.
steps.lean: hc discharges the sign from hκ. hlow/hupp scale hcross. The first conjunction proves real Hermitianity, equivalently symmetry.

units.lean_statement: The statement uses IsHermitian over ℝ and explicit universal dot-product inequalities, avoiding entrywise matrix order and the default Pi norm.
units.lean_proof: The checked proof follows the source orthogonality → Cauchy–Schwarz → quadratic expansion route.
